title: Reference-image interpretation and inferred design language
note: Images are treated as sources of transferable geometric/topological principles, not as literal templates. Each principle lists the visual motivation, the abstraction, its atomistic realisation in graphene-derived carbon, required assumptions and plausible alternative readings. All entries are editable in the application; regenerating structures uses the mapping in 'families'.

images.visual_features: A thick primary vein with secondary and tertiary branches; the finest veins close into a reticulate network of polygonal areoles; 3-4 distinct vein widths; closed loops at every level; overall anisotropy set by the midrib.
principles: P1 multi-level (nested) network hierarchy with a large width ratio between levels
P2 closed loops (redundancy) at every level
P4 global anisotropy of the primary load path

images.short: closed-cell walls with fine open branching inside cells
images.visual_features: Thick yellow cell walls form a polygonal foam-like closed network; each cell contains a much finer, open (tree-like) network; two well separated length scales (ratio ~5-10); the coarse level is closed-cell, the fine level is open/branching.
principles: P1 two-level hierarchy with distinct topology per level (closed coarse net, open fine net)
P3 compartmentalisation: coarse walls isolate domains

images.visual_features: Slender fibres forming an irregular polygonal mesh; cell sizes vary; several nets are overlaid (redundant, layered); paths are curved and tortuous; no straight through-going lines.
principles: P6 disorder in cell size/shape (polygonal, Voronoi-like)
P2 redundancy by overlaid/duplicated load paths
P7 tortuous, curved load paths with slender uniform ligaments

images.visual_features: Straight fibres crossing at several fixed angles, forming triangles/quadrilaterals; through-going lines span the whole field; nodes where 3-4 lines meet; some fibres thicker than others.
principles: P8 straight through-going load paths aligned with a few directions (load-path organisation)
P4 strong anisotropy / orientation relative to the load
P9 high-connectivity nodes (stiff triangulated topology) vs. low-connectivity (bending-dominated) topologies

images.short: nested rings around a central void, size gradient
images.visual_features: Concentric, nested polygonal rings converge on a central hole; ring cells shrink toward the centre; radial and circumferential connections; a defect (hole) surrounded by a graded, compliant halo.
principles: P10 spatial gradients of cell size (graded architecture)
P11 nesting around a flaw: local architecture organised around a defect (flaw shielding / crack arrest hypothesis)

P1.name: nested hierarchy
P1.abstraction: structure at n > 1 well separated length scales, each level a network of ligaments enclosing pores; levels differ in ligament width and pore size by a scale ratio r
P1.atomistic_realisation: graphene nanomesh whose pore pattern has several characteristic periods: fine pores (d1, period p1) inside domains bounded by wider 'vein' ligaments (width W2, domain size D2); optional third level (W3, D3). Hierarchy depth = number of levels; scale ratio = D2/p1; inter-level connectivity = fine ligaments attached to veins
P1.assumptions: ligaments >= ~5 A wide remain stable sp2 carbon; pores are formed by atom removal followed by relaxation; periodic supercells impose a maximal coarse scale
P1.alternatives: hierarchy could instead be expressed through graded ligament widths without domains, or through hierarchical defects (vacancy clusters at two scales)

P2.name: redundancy / loops
P2.abstraction: multiple independent load paths (cyclomatic number of the ligament graph)
P2.atomistic_realisation: compare closed-cell meshes (many loops) with open/branching or slit patterns at the same porosity; descriptor cyclomatic_per_atom
P2.assumptions: loop count is measured on the bond graph of the relaxed structure
P2.alternatives: redundancy via multiple layers is not accessible in a single sheet; represented in-plane only

P3.name: compartmentalisation
P3.abstraction: coarse walls isolate domains so that damage inside one domain need not propagate
P3.atomistic_realisation: vein network of the two-level nanomesh; test whether cracks stop at veins
P3.assumptions: vein width sets the barrier strength
P3.alternatives: walls may act as stress concentrators instead of barriers

P4.name: anisotropy / orientation
P4.abstraction: principal ligament direction relative to the load
P4.atomistic_realisation: slit arrays and elliptical pores at 0/45/90 degrees to the tensile axis; strut lattices with and without a strut family along the load; zigzag vs armchair lattice orientation
P4.alternatives: anisotropy from the graphene lattice itself (chirality) is a separate, atomistic-scale source of anisotropy

P5.name: scale separation
P5.abstraction: ratio of the characteristic sizes of successive levels
P5.atomistic_realisation: vary domain size D2 at fixed fine period p1 (ratio 2..6)
P5.assumptions: cell size must accommodate several domains
P5.alternatives: graded (continuous) rather than discrete scale separation

P6.name: disorder
P6.abstraction: randomness of pore position, size and cell shape
P6.atomistic_realisation: jittered / size-dispersed pore lattices, periodic Voronoi ligament networks with tunable regularity; multiple seeds
P6.alternatives: disorder in ligament width instead of pore position

P7.name: tortuous load paths
P7.abstraction: load paths longer than the straight distance (tortuosity)
P7.atomistic_realisation: Voronoi networks and staggered pore lattices; descriptor tortuosity_x
P7.assumptions: tortuosity measured on the bond graph
P7.alternatives: tortuosity could be imposed by wavy slits

P8.name: straight through-going load paths
P8.abstraction: continuous ligaments spanning the cell along the load
P8.atomistic_realisation: strut lattices with a strut family at 0 degrees vs none; slits parallel to the load

P9.name: node connectivity
P9.abstraction: number of ligaments meeting at nodes (triangulated vs polygonal)
P9.atomistic_realisation: 0/60/120 strut lattice (6-connected nodes) vs 0/90 (4-connected) vs honeycomb-like Voronoi (3-connected)
P9.assumptions: at the nanoscale ligaments are plates, not beams; stretching dominates
P9.alternatives: connectivity effects may be masked by stress concentration at nodes

P10.name: gradients
P10.abstraction: smooth spatial variation of pore size / porosity
P10.atomistic_realisation: pore-size gradient along x or radially (graded_pores family)
P10.assumptions: gradient wavelength limited by the cell
P10.alternatives: gradient of ligament width at constant pore size

P11.name: nesting around a flaw
P11.abstraction: a central flaw surrounded by concentric rings of smaller pores (compliant halo)
P11.atomistic_realisation: ring_around_hole family: hole + n rings of small pores, compared with the bare hole and with hole + uniform background pores at matched porosity
P11.assumptions: the halo changes the stress field at the hole edge
P11.alternatives: rings may simply add more crack nuclei

major_design_variables: disorder amplitude (jitter, size dispersion, Voronoi regularity)
anisotropy / orientation of pores or struts
